options.why: Divided the original length by the image length — the scale factor is image divided by original.
Found the difference between the widths, $10-5=5$; a scale factor compares sides by division, not subtraction.
Divided the original length by the image length — for a reduction the image goes on top, giving a factor less than $1$.
Used the difference $10-4=6$ over the original, $\frac{6}{10}$; the factor is the image length itself divided by the original.

questions.question_text: A figure is enlarged by a scale factor of $2.5$. A side of the original is $6$ cm long. How long is the corresponding side of the image?

options.why: Divided by the scale factor instead of multiplying — that finds an original from an image, not the other way round.
Added the scale factor to the length; scaling multiplies every side, it does not add a fixed amount.

questions.question_text: A figure is enlarged by a scale factor of $4$. A side of the image is $26$ cm long. How long is the corresponding side of the original?

options.why: Multiplied by the scale factor, but $26$ cm is already the image — divide by $4$ to get back to the original.
Subtracted the scale factor from the length; the original is found by dividing, not subtracting.

questions.question_text: The scale factor from a figure to its image is $\frac{7}{5}$. Which statement describes the image?

options.text: It is an enlargement of the original.
It is a reduction of the original.
options.why: Assumed a fractional scale factor always reduces; $\frac{7}{5}$ is greater than $1$, so it enlarges.

options.text: It is congruent to the original.
options.why: Only a scale factor of exactly $1$ gives a congruent image, and $\frac{7}{5}\neq1$.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{7}{5}=1.4>1$
A scale factor greater than $1$ gives an enlargement.

questions.question_text: A figure with a perimeter of $23$ cm is enlarged by a scale factor of $2$. What is the perimeter of the image?

options.why: Multiplied by the scale factor twice — that is what happens to area, not perimeter.
Added the scale factor to the perimeter; every side is multiplied by $2$, so the perimeter is too.
Assumed the perimeter stays the same; perimeter is a length, so it is also multiplied by the scale factor.

questions.solution_text:
Every side is multiplied by $2$, so the perimeter is too.
$P=23\times2$
$=46\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text: A side of the original figure is $5$ cm long, and the corresponding side of the image is $1.5$ m long. What is the scale factor?

options.why: Divided $1.5$ by $5$ without converting to the same unit first — $1.5$ m is $150$ cm.
Converted $1.5$ m to $15$ cm instead of $150$ cm before dividing — one metre is $100$ cm.

questions.question_text: A regular pentagon is enlarged by a scale factor of $4$. The image has a perimeter of $90$ cm. What is the side length of the original pentagon?

options.why: This is the image's side length ($90\div5$) — the original's side still needs dividing by the scale factor.
This is the original's perimeter ($90\div4$) — the question asks for one side, so divide by the $5$ sides as well.

questions.question_text: A figure is enlarged by a scale factor of $4$, and the image is then reduced by a scale factor of $0.25$. What single scale factor takes the first figure to the final image?

options.why: Added the two scale factors; successive scalings multiply, so the overall factor is $4\times0.25$.
Subtracted the second factor from the first; successive scalings combine by multiplication, not subtraction.
